en: So when using Ollama through the command
line, as I showed it to you earlier,
you can chat with it and you will build a
chat history here, of course.
What you can also do is configure it with
help of various slash commands and you can
always type slash question mark to see a
list of the available commands.
For example, you can use slash show to view
some information about the currently running
model.
With show info, for example, you get a brief
overview of the model architecture. So the
model family, you could say, Gemma 3 in my
case, the number of parameters, the
available context length for this model, the
quantization used, and some other pieces of
information. Like for example, the
parameters that have been set for this
running instance of the model, so to say. So
the parameters that are currently active for
this chat session.
One word about the context length, by the
way. This can be misleading because that is
the actual context length supported by this
model. It is not, however, necessarily the
context length that has been set for your
currently running chat session.
And I'll get back to how to control that in
just a second.
But that is something to note. This is just
the maximum context length, not the
currently active one.
You also see the capabilities like text
completion and in case of the Gemma models,
also vision so that it can analyze images.
And there's of course more you can inspect
about this model.
Show license shows you, well, the license,
though here it fails to grab that. It's
always a good idea to check Hugging Face for
that then to make sure that you're
respecting the license.
And show parameters shows you the currently
set parameters. Now you might wonder
who set parameters because you didn't, you
did not see me set any parameters here. And
for that, you can go back to that Ollama
model detail page on their website. And
there you'll find this params
area here.
And if you click on that, you'll actually
see
a set of parameters which will be different
for each model, or which can be different
for each model, I should say.
And these parameters are simply set
automatically whenever you run a model. You
can override them, but these are default
parameters that are set whenever you start a
model with Ollama.
And that's just something to be aware of,
and therefore this
is what you also see
here.
By the way, I'll get back to this weird stop
thing here later.
You already know top_p, temperature, and
top_k from the LM Studio section. In case
you don't, attached you find a link to that
lecture where I explain those parameters.
What's also interesting is show system,
which shows you the system prompt that was
specified for this model. And here you see
that no system message has been specified.
That is of course something you can change,
but here, as you see for this model, no
system message has been set. And later you
will learn how you can set a default system
message for an entire model that will then
apply to all chat sessions started based on
that model.
